title: MEPS 2024: annual hours U.S. adults spend on health care time and paperwork
unit: hours per year per adult (mean over adults with a valid answer), or percent of adults
definition: Edited annual hours adults report spending on their own visits and prescriptions, on others' visits, on medical bills and insurance, and on health care paperwork; plus the share who cared for a friend or family member in the past 30 days. Reported per week, month or year and converted to hours per year.
method: Weighted mean (ESAQ person weight ESAQWT24F) with a Taylor-linearised standard error from VARSTR and VARPSU; adults who skipped an item are excluded from that item.
source_locator: MEPS HC-256 (2024 Full-Year Consolidated): EQMVAM53, EQOVAM53, EQMBAM53, EQPPAM53, EQCARE53, ESAQWT24F
comparability: All U.S. adults who answered the questionnaire, not people with Lyme disease or Long COVID: MEPS cannot identify either condition reliably (AHRQ, 2026-09-24).
Fielded in 2024 only: the questionnaire was funded for that year, so there is no trend and no later update.

Self-reported. MEPS top-coded the annual hours at the 99.5th percentile (Table 13 of the HC-256 documentation: 2,080 hours for own visits, 1,040 for others' visits, 720 for bills, 520 for paperwork), so a few very large values are capped. About 6% of respondents skipped each time item, and MEPS notes that about 20% of those who completed the paper version gave no answer to them.
Hours, not dollars. Converting hours to dollars needs a published wage or value-of-time source shown next to the estimate.

summary: own medical visits and filling prescriptions: 60.6 hours a year; medical visits and prescriptions for other people: 30.4 hours a year; paying or managing medical bills and insurance: 18.9 hours a year; health care paperwork: finding doctors, understanding plans, getting approvals: 15.5 hours a year; 15.9% of adults cared for someone in the past 30 days.
how_to_use: Context for administrative and care-navigation burden and for caregiving in any document; a general adult benchmark, never a Lyme or Long COVID figure.

provenance.collection_note: Respondent-reported conditions and hours, coded to ICD-10 by MEPS abstractors; not a clinical record.
provenance.computed_by: Computed in code from the federal file; no AI model
provenance.relevance: All U.S. adults who answered the questionnaire, not people with Lyme disease or Long COVID: MEPS cannot identify either condition reliably (AHRQ, 2026-09-24).
provenance.reliability: About 11,600 adults, design-based standard errors; about 6% skipped each time item.
